scope: In-process cache of actual PostgreSQL retrieval rows. Not a generated-answer cache, distributed cache, latency benchmark or new index activation.
matrix: 22 sequential authored cases; 8 hits,13 misses including2 SQL errors,1 expiry. Actual monotonic clock, TTL3000ms; wait3100ms before expiry case.
authority: Principal and cache_state loaded from database under real role inside REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY. cache_state is admin-owned SELECT-only for application. Missing trusted scope rejects key.
indexRevision: SHA256 of original corpus.json and schema.sql bytes with explicit separator; fixed for this experiment. No new index version claimed.
invalidation: Revoke alpha_manager increments principal revision2; restore increments3. Document ACL update and global accessRevision2 commit atomically before new request. Old cache entries are logically unreachable under new key,not magically erased.
clock: performance.now; timestamps only meaningful within capture process. TTL expiry observed by native waiting. Unit fake-clock controls labeled separately.
errors: Two SELECT1/0 attempts have SQLSTATE22012, both lookup miss and both actual source queries; errors never inserted.
limits: One process, one sequential workload, source SQL counts exclude principal/state/identity queries, known synthetic data, no concurrent revocation guarantee or stampede test. Bounded FIFO128entries, native workload does not reach eviction.
preservation: Existing success/failure artifact refuses overwrite. New experiment requires different files/protocol.
